title: Prior and future rain slopes did not differ clearly for Aedes vexans catch share in four US samples in 2016-2019 and 2021-2024
abstract: We tested whether rain before capture had a more positive link than rain after capture to Aedes vexans share among identified female mosquitoes. Four tests use NEON RELEASE-2026 and Daymet V4 R1 in eastern and western US sites in 2016-2019 and 2021-2024. Weighted plot-month and plot-year models use 11,968 traps in 2,048 site-dates at 39 sites. Rain windows cover 8-28 days before and after capture. Prior slopes minus future slopes were +1.382, +1.610, +0.086 and -0.178 percentage points per doubling of one plus rain total in mm. All four adjusted site/year intervals include zero. All planned model checks also gave intervals across zero. Eastern site-deletion estimates stayed positive; western ranges crossed zero. These records do not establish a common lagged rainfall link or its absence. Positive-catch selection, species-specific capture, rare western catches, a curated source and only four years per period limit inference. The package gives code, two figures, source hashes, aggregate checks and a tested external-data rebuild. It tests no pollution, disease outcome or causal climate-change effect.

display.caption: Prior rain slopes minus future rain slopes. Solid intervals use site and year clusters. Dashed intervals use site clusters only. Each family has a four-test correction. All primary intervals include zero.
Weighted catch share and residual rain-contrast variation in each primary sample. Western catches have low focal shares. Controls retain 23-46 percent of the original contrast variation.

citations.reason: Adapt retrieval and sample selection code and exact input metadata. The new test uses a named species share, plot effects and a primary prior-minus-future rainfall contrast.
Original source metadata and integer-count recovery approach, reused through the rain study. These records overlap, so this is not independent source validation.
Prior capture-temperature timing test motivates a distinct rainfall timing contrast for composition.
Independent Manitoba field study found species-specific weather links. Our share outcome and lag window differ from its count models.
